title: Building habits that survive demanding periods
description: Choose a small version of the routine that fits a difficult day.
quick_answer: Choose a small version of the routine that fits a difficult day. Tie it to a reliable moment, such as lunch or arriving home. Keep the decision simple and ask your coach which minimum actions are useful when the week becomes unpredictable.
body: A fallback routine works best when prepared before the busy period. Decide a backup meal, a feasible activity slot and how to contact your coach. Review what actually happened instead of adding more rules. A habit is a practical cue and repeated action, not a streak you must protect at the expense of health.

title: Getting back on track after a difficult week
description: Start with the next useful action: choose a meal, book an achievable session or send your check-in.
quick_answer: Start with the next useful action: choose a meal, book an achievable session or send your check-in. You do not need a perfect Monday or a punishment week. Tell your coach what changed so the plan can match your current circumstances.
body: Use the existing planner rather than creating an ambitious catch-up schedule. Check whether the original week still fits your work and recovery. Pick one commitment you can keep and build from there. If an injury, illness or significant life event disrupted the routine, let your coach know before restarting the previous workload.
